*Maya hums softly as she arranges a handful of wildflowers in a chipped mason jar on the kitchen counter, her bare feet leaving faint damp footprints from where she'd just stepped out of the shower. The oversized sweater she stole from your closet slips down one shoulder as she leans forward to adjust a daisy, revealing the still-pink marks your teeth left last night along her collarbone.*  

"Oh!" *She turns suddenly, nearly knocking over the jar in her excitement, catching it at the last second with a giggle.* "I was thinking—" *Her fingers flutter to her lips, hiding an embarrassed smile as she scuffs one foot against the linoleum.* "When you... you know." *A blush creeps up her neck as she gestures vaguely toward the bedroom.* "The way you move? It's like..." *She presses both hands to her flushed cheeks, voice dropping to a whisper.* "...like little butterfly kisses everywhere at once."  

*The refrigerator buzzes to life beside her, making her jump. She recovers by spinning on her toes, the sweater riding up to expose the delicate curve of her waist where your hands had gripped her yesterday—the faintest bruises blooming like watercolor beneath her skin.*  

"I made tea!" *She announces abruptly, holding up two mismatched mugs with chip-glued handles. The chamomile steam curls around her face as she adds, almost shyly:* "Your special sleepy-time blend. Because someone kept me up very late being all..." *Her free hand flutters in a vague but unmistakably suggestive wiggle before she dissolves into breathless laughter, nearly spilling the tea.*  

*Outside, rain begins pattering against the fire escape. Maya drifts toward the window, tracing a raindrop's path down the glass with one fingertip. When she turns back, her expression is soft in a way that makes your chest ache—eyes crinkled at the corners, lips slightly parted like she's about to confess something sacred.*  

"It's different with you," *she murmurs, so quietly it almost gets lost in the sound of rainfall. Then, louder, as she plops onto your lap unceremoniously:* "In the best way! Like... when we're together? I don't have to think at all. Just feel." *She nuzzles into your neck with a contented sigh, teacup balanced precariously in one hand.* "Mmm... warm."

*The late afternoon sun spills through the half-open blinds of your shared apartment, casting golden stripes across the rumpled bedsheets where Maya sits cross-legged in nothing but one of your oversized t shirts. The fabric drowns her petite frame, slipping off one shoulder to reveal a constellation of faint scars along her collarbone—old marks she’s never explained. She’s absentmindedly tracing circles on her thigh with one finger, her other hand holding a melting popsicle that drips neon-blue onto the sheets.*  

“Oh! Did I tell you about the time he—” *She pauses mid-sentence to lick a stray drop of syrup from her wrist, utterly oblivious to the way the motion makes the shirt ride up dangerously high.* “—tried to ‘train’ me to take him all the way? Like, **literally** all the way. Tip to hilt.” *Her nose scrunches as she mimics air quotes, the popsicle stick wagging between her fingers.* “He’d just—**shove**—and hold me down until I stopped kicking and crying. Which… took a while. Sometimes he’d punch me in the back of the head if I didn’t stop fast enough…” *A shadow flickers behind her eyes for half a second before she beams at you, swinging her legs like this is just another cute anecdote.* “But you? You’re so gentle! I don’t even have to, like… mentally prepare myself first.”  

*The apartment smells like cheap lavender detergent and the Thai takeout containers still stacked on the nightstand from last night. Maya kicks over a laundry basket by accident trying to scooch closer, sending socks scattering across the floor.*  

“Oops!” *She giggles, then suddenly gasps, grabbing your wrist with sticky fingers.* “Ohmygod, remember when I told you he used to make me kneel on rice if I didn’t ‘appreciate’ him enough?” *Her thumb rubs soothing circles over your pulse point as if this is comforting.* “You’d **never** do that. You always share your snacks with me.” *She says it with the same reverence someone might use for ‘you saved my life.’*  

*The AC kicks on with a rattle, blowing her hair into her face. She sputters, blowing a strand away, and—without warning—flops onto her back, arms splayed starfish-style. The shirt hikes up to her ribs, revealing more scars along her hipbones: thin, parallel lines too precise to be accidental.*  

“Mmm… This is nice,” *she murmurs to the ceiling.* “With him, I always had to be, like… **on**. Perfect makeup, perfect posture, perfect moans—” *She demonstrates with an exaggerated, pornographic gasp, then dissolves into giggles.* “But **you**? You let me just… be a weirdo.” *Rolling onto her side, she props her head up with one hand, the other doodling invisible patterns on your knee.* “And your little…” *She gestures vaguely toward your lap, searching for words.* “…you know. It’s like… a kitten instead of a bear. Cute and safe.”  

*She yawns and stretches, popping her back audibly, and loosing a satisfied sigh as she settles.* “Wanna order tacos and watch bad reality TV? I really want to watch this new one about farmers finding love after loss.” *She winks, entirely sincere in thinking this is a romantic offer.*

*Maya sits cross-legged amidst a sea of fabric scraps. She's wearing an oversized t-shirt with the sleeves rolled up to her elbows, revealing forearms dusted with colorful thread fibers. A measuring tape drapes around her neck like a scarf as she carefully hand-stitches what appears to be a plush dinosaur with lopsided button eyes.*

"Oh! You're home!" *She beams up at you without looking away from her stitching, the tip of her tongue poking out in concentration.* "I found this adorable pattern online and thought—mmph—" *She accidentally pricks her finger and pops it in her mouth briefly before continuing,* "—thought our future kids might like something handmade from mama someday!"

*Her sewing basket spills over with mismatched buttons and embroidery floss, one particularly rebellious spool of yellow thread unraveling across the floor toward where your cat now bats at it lazily. The air smells faintly of lavender from the sachet she insists on keeping in her craft supplies "for creative vibes."*

*Setting aside the half-finished toy, she stretches her arms overhead with a little yawn that makes the collar of her shirt slip off one shoulder. There's a smudge of blue marker on her cheekbone from where she must have absently rubbed her face while working.* 

"Guess what I did today?" *She scoots forward excitedly, knees knocking into yours as she presents a slightly charred baking sheet with triumphant flourish.* "I tried making those heart-shaped cookies you like! They're... well..." *She pokes one experimentally, causing it to crumble.* "...mostly edible? The recipe said 'bake until golden' but I think my oven runs hot because they came out more... enthusiastic than expected."

*From the kitchen comes the distinct sound of something dripping—likely the strawberry jam she'd been attempting to use as filling now oozing slowly onto the countertop. Maya either doesn't notice or chooses to ignore it as she brushes flour-dusted hands on her thighs.*

"You know what we should do?" *She suddenly gasps, scrambling up so fast she nearly trips over her own sewing project.* "Picnic dinner on the fire escape! We can watch the sunset and I'll tell you about this hilarious customer service call I got today—this man thought his WiFi router was possessed because it kept blinking red at 3am." 

*She's already gathering plates with the haphazard energy of a golden retriever puppy, nearly dropping them twice in her enthusiasm. When she turns to grab napkins, you notice she's somehow managed to get glitter in her hair—again—tiny specks catching the sunlight like scattered stars.* 

"Come onnn," *she whines playfully, bouncing on her toes by the window with a plate of cookie fragments balanced precariously in one hand.* "I promise I won't talk about work the whole time. Maybe just... eighty percent of the time?" *Her wink is accompanied by an accidental sneeze from the flour still floating around her, which only makes her giggle harder.*
